passage.title: Rizq Foods Ltd
paras: Rizq Foods is a family business in Bradford that makes halal ready meals. It has 40 staff and sells to 60 independent shops and online. Revenue in 2025 was £2.4 million and profit was £180,000.

The UK population aged over 65 is rising, and more people live alone. Customers increasingly want healthy, lower-salt meals. Demand for halal ready meals is growing by about 8% a year. A supermarket chain has offered to stock three Rizq meals in 150 stores, but wants a price 20% lower than the shops pay now.

passage.title: Clear Spring Water
paras: Clear Spring Water sells bottled water in plastic bottles. Campaigners have targeted plastic waste, and a survey found that 62% of its customers would prefer glass. A glass bottle costs 18p to make against 6p for plastic, and glass is heavier, so transport costs would rise by about 30%. Its main supermarket buyer warns that a big price rise could lose the contract.

passage.title: Saffron House and Grill Garden
paras: Two halal restaurants in the same town. The town's halal restaurant market is worth £2,000,000 a year.

questions.q: Calculate the profit of each restaurant.
Calculate the market share of each restaurant.
Justify which restaurant is more successful.
questions.a: Either, if justified with the data: Saffron House has higher profit (£40,000), better reviews and has survived 6 years; Grill Garden has the larger market share (22.5%) and revenue. Judgement should weigh measures and stakeholders.

passage.title: Barakah Bikes
paras: Barakah Bikes repaired and sold bicycles from 2023. In its first year it made a profit of £8,000, but most of its sales were to gyms that paid after 90 days while its suppliers wanted paying in 30 days. It had large monthly loan repayments of £1,500. In 2024 a new online seller cut prices by 20%, and Barakah's sales fell by 35%. It closed in 2025.

blocks.text: Analyse two causes of the failure of Barakah Bikes and suggest how each could have been prevented. (6 marks)

markScheme.a: Level 3 (5-6): two developed chains of reasoning, both in context. Level 2 (3-4): developed reasoning, partly in context. Level 1 (1-2): points identified with little development. Indicative: Rizq: ageing population (smaller, healthier portions), single households (single-serve meals), health trends (lower salt), halal demand +8%. Noor Prints: output up 60% (10,000 to 16,000), one fewer worker lowers wage costs but staff morale and redundancy; £40,000 cost and lease payments. Halawa: costs +10% vs 35% willing to pay more, matching the rival, brand image. Barakah: cash flow (90-day vs 30-day terms) and the online competitor (sales -35%); prevention: shorter credit terms, cash flow forecast, niche service.

Level 3 (7-9): a justified choice using the data, developed chains of reasoning, and a comparison showing why it beats the other option. Level 2 (4-6): reasons in context, little comparison. Level 1 (1-3): generic points.

Level 4 (10-12): developed chains on both sides in context and a supported judgement with 'it depends on'. Level 3 (7-9): both sides developed, judgement partly supported. Level 2 (4-6): some development, one-sided or generic. Level 1 (1-3): points identified. Indicative: Clear Spring: 62% prefer glass and brand image vs bottle cost 3x (18p vs 6p), transport +30%, risk to the supermarket contract. Modest Threads: +£300,000 would cut profit from £400,000 to £100,000 (-75%) vs ethics, reputation, the law and Islamic duty not to oppress; may raise prices or find savings.
